items.actClause: AN ACT in relation to authorizing and directing the public service commission to study the impact on consumers and perform a cost benefit analysis of the Reforming the Energy Vision (REV) initiative
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4423

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act in relation to authorizing and directing the public service
commission to study the impact on consumers and perform a cost benefit
analysis of the Reforming the Energy Vision (REV) initiative

 PURPOSE OF BILL :

This bill would authorize and direct the public service commission to
study the impact on consumers and perform a cost benefit analysis of
the REV initiative.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 -- Such study and analysis performed by the public service
commission to study the impact on consumers and perform a cost benefit
analysis of the Reforming the Energy Vision (REV) initiative shall
include, but not be limited to:

1) analysis of the potential benefits and costs of the REV initiative;

2) the impact of REV on electric rates charged to consumers through
additional taxes and fees, increased rates or any charges required to
fund the REV initiative;

3) the feasibility of other potential initiatives and approaches to
upgrading and updating the current energy infrastructure;

4) an analysis of potential benefits and costs of such other
initiatives determined feasible pursuant to subdivision three of this
section;

5) the impact on consumers resulting from the cost and expense of
replacing existing energy infrastructure; and

6) any other information the public service commission deems
necessary.

Section 2 - The public service commission shall report its finds to
the Governor, the Temporary President of the Senate, the Speaker of
the Assembly, the Minority Leaders of the Senate and the Assembly on
or before one year after the effective date of this act.

Section 3 - No additional taxes and fees, increased rates or any other
charges required to fund the REV initiative shall be imposed upon
existing utility rates and charges of consumers of this state until
the completion of the study, analysis and report set forth in this
act.

Section 4 - Effective date

 JUSTIFICATION :

The full details of The Energy Highway and REV initiatives have not
yet been fully disclosed. This legislation would require a fiscal
analysis and provide more transparency for what has the potential to
be a multi-billion dollar initiative.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

S.5131/A.7808 - 2015-2016

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Nominal

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public service law and the public authorities law, in relation to oversight by the New York state public authorities control board
A.lawCode: Add §5-a, Pub Serv L; amd §§1854 & 51, Pub Auth L
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4423A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the public service law and the public authorities law,
in relation to oversight by the New York state public authorities
control board

 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :

This bill would increase Legislative oversight over the New York State
Public Service Commission (PSC) and the New York State Energy Research
and Development Authority (NYSERDA).

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill would require the PSC to obtain approval from
the New York State Public Authorities Control Board (PACE) for the
following actions by the PSC:

- an increase in rates, charges, surcharges, assessments, fees,
levies, or any other collections, which would increase costs for
ratepayers by more than $700,000; collected solely for and directed to
NYSERDA the PACB's jurisdiction would apply to these activities that
amount to a total of $700,000, regardless of whether they are
implemented through a single action or a series of actions, as
described in the bill; and/or

- a transfer, repurposing, reprogramming, or any other action that
would change the use of money directed to NYSERDA previously
designated or intended for a different purpose.

The PSC would conduct a cost-benefit analysis of the public benefit of
these actions and would provide the analysis to the PACB, along with
the PSC's application to the PACB for approval of the actions.

Section 2 of the bill would require a similar approval process by the
PACE of NYSERDA's activities in the area of any transfer, repurposing,
reprogramming, or any other action that would change the use of money
previously designated or intended for a different purpose.

Section 3 of the bill would add the PSC to the list of entities that
are subject to the PACB's jurisdiction.

Section 4 of the bill would expand the PACB's decision-making criteria
to include a determination that a cost-benefit analysis of the actions
regulated by this bill shows that those actions are in the public
interest.

Section 5 of the bill states that these provisions would be effective
as of June 25, 2015.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The Legislature finds that its delegation of ratemaking authority to
the PSC would benefit from additional supervision by the PACB in order
to provide oversight over the PSC' s actions to impose very large
costs on ratepayers or to transfer funds away from their original
purposes. Additionally, this PACB oversight should be extended to
NYSERDA, as the Authority also is involved in the repurposing of
funds.

Through its appointments to the PACE, the Legislature will ensure that
these actions by the PSC and NYSERDA are in the public interest. The
Legislature has a just role in the approval of transactions that

involve very large sums of money in order to ensure the best outcome
for ratepayers.

New bill

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Nominal

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

B.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to directing the public service commission to conduct a study of the Reforming the Energy Vision initiative
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4423B

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the public service law, in relation
to directing the public service commission to conduct a study of the
Reforming the Energy Vision initiative

 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :

This bill would direct a study of the Reforming the Energy Vision
initiative by the public service commission.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 - Amends the public service law by adding a new section
66-o.

Section 2 - Establishes the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This bill seeks data to determine the benefits and cost of
effectiveness of REV.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016 - S.5131/A./7808

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Nominal

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
